prompt:
Classify this frame into exactly one class from this list. These are the classes and their definitions, verbatim from the human labeller's rubric:

GOOD: a gallery-worthy detail frame of the build
ok: usable, not the best pose of its build
ok-texel: usable but texels visible (camera too close, texture resolution showing)
ok-cropped: usable; the subject's top is cut off
dull: shaded flat wall; nothing to look at
dark: underexposed close-up
BAD-roof: camera inside a roof or wall; flat planes
BAD-mist: Mistlands mist volume; the frame is fogged out
BAD-skyladder: linear build (ladder to a sky bucket); aim is empty sky
BAD-ladder: linear build (rope-ladder diagonal) in haze; aim is empty air
BAD-aim-water: aim is open water; the build is at the frame edge or absent
BAD-dark-texel: shaded close-up with texels visible

Also give a tier rollup: "GOOD" only for the GOOD class, "ok" for ok/ok-texel/ok-cropped/dull/dark, "BAD" for any BAD-* class.

Respond with exactly this JSON and nothing else:
{"tier": "<GOOD|ok|BAD>", "class": "<one class name from the list>", "reason": "<one short sentence>"}
system: You are judging automated architectural photographs of player-built structures in the game Valheim. Each frame is a "detail" shot: the camera was solved to put a target pixels-per-metre on part of a building, so a partial view of a large build is intended, not a fault. The frames go into a public gallery that celebrates what players built. You are judging photographs of architecture, not screenshots of gameplay. Answer only with the requested JSON.
